man.title: The manifesto
man.p1: Artificial intelligence and robotics are advancing fast, but it would be unwise to treat the disappearance of almost all jobs as certain. Recent research points above all to an uneven transformation of tasks, skills and the way work is organized.
man.p2: The International Labour Organization estimates that about one job in four is potentially exposed to generative AI, while judging transformation more likely than full replacement. The Future of Jobs Report 2025 anticipates 170 million jobs created and 92 million eliminated by 2030. These figures are not certainties: creation, displacement and reskilling can happen at the same time.
man.idea: Don't try to beat AI at its own speed, and don't ignore it. Learn to hand it what it does well, to check what it does imperfectly, and to strengthen what demands context, relationship, responsibility, creativity and judgment.
man.sources: Sources: International Labour Organization (ILO); World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025.
ax.title: Three ways to thrive with AI
ax.a1_desc: Hand AI what it does well: draft text, automate repetitive tasks, explore data. You learn to steer it (prompting) and pick the right tools.
ax.a2_desc: Control what it does imperfectly: check its answers, spot errors and bias, trace the sources. This is the heart of critical thinking.
ax.a3_desc: Grow what AI doesn't replace: judgment, creativity, communication, the ability to lead and create, relationship and responsibility.

priv.p1: This page says what Lojik360 does with your data. It is short because there is little to say: the site is almost entirely static, it sets no cookies and uses no analytics.
priv.p2: Your e-mail address, if you subscribe to the newsletter. It goes to an Atmart LLC server (a Cloudflare Worker) and is stored there with the date, the language and the page you came from. It is kept until you ask us to delete it — we set no automatic expiry, and we would rather say so than announce a deadline nothing would enforce.
priv.p3: What you write to the assistant (the chat bubble, on 24 pages). Your messages are passed to an AI model to produce the answer. They are not stored anywhere: our server hands them to the model and keeps no copy.
priv.p4: Your IP address, kept for about 25 hours in a counter that limits abuse (mass sign-ups, automated requests). It is not linked to your e-mail or your messages, and it expires on its own.
priv.p5: Your comments, on the five tutorial pages that offer them. They are handled by Cusdis, a third-party service: what you write there follows their policy, not ours.
priv.p6: Three things, and they never leave: the language you chose, the light or dark background, and the quizzes you finished. They live in your device's local storage. Clearing site data removes them, and breaks nothing.
priv.p7: The Lojikkid pages are written for children. They carry neither the assistant nor comments, and collect nothing. The newsletter is for adults: please do not use it to sign a child up.
priv.h2d: Your rights, and how to use them
priv.p8: Write to sales@atmart.ltd to find out what we hold about you, correct it, or have it deleted. A request to remove you from the newsletter is applied without discussion and without questions. We sell nothing, we share nothing for advertising, and we run no ads.
